clue.text: Fruit's inexpensive unit cost?

parts.note: a single penny, abbreviated p, is about as cheap a price as there is
a price quoted per unit is so much each

explanation.surface: A shopper asks whether this fruit is cheap per item.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link ('is'). 'Inexpensive unit cost' reads as 'p each', a penny apiece, in old pre-decimal-feeling shop language.
explanation.definitionFit: A peach is a soft stone fruit with downy skin.

clue.text: In city, annoyance about parking is localised

parts.note: Paris is the French capital city

indicators.note: about means the annoyance word wraps around the parking letter

parts.note: the hump is British slang for a fit of annoyance, as in 'get the hump'
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: In a city, irritation about parking is a local issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link here, not a container. Parish pump, as an adjective, describes petty village concerns; 'get the hump' is British for becoming sulky.
explanation.definitionFit: Parish-pump politics are parochial, concerned only with narrow local matters, so the phrase means localised.

clue.text: An expression of admiration for so-called little woman

parts.note: 'My!' is an exclamation of surprise or admiration

explanation.surface: Someone praises a petite woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so-called' flags that 'little woman' is a title: Amy March is one of Louisa May Alcott's Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: Amy is the youngest March sister in the novel Little Women.

clue.text: Famous consultant working on cases with GP

definitions.text: Famous consultant working on cases with GP

parts.words: Famous consultant working on cases with GP
parts.note: the consultant is not a hospital doctor but the fictional consulting detective, whose cases he shares with his friend Dr Watson, a general practitioner

explanation.surface: A well-known hospital specialist treats patients alongside a family doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consultant' and 'GP' paint a medical picture, but the cases are crimes and the GP is Dr Watson.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherlock Holmes called himself the world's only consulting detective, partnered by Dr Watson.

clue.text: The point of this fastening device is not obvious

definitions.text: The point of this fastening device is not obvious

parts.words: The point of this fastening device is not obvious
parts.note: the pin's sharp point tucks under a guard so it is literally hidden, while 'point' pretends to mean purpose

explanation.surface: Someone can't see what a particular fastener is for.
explanation.definitionFit: This pin closes with its sharp tip covered by a clasp, an example of a fastening device whose point stays out of sight.

clue.text: Tailor has extremely rearranged something to wear on top

indicators.note: the letters of tailor has are thoroughly reordered

explanation.surface: A tailor has thoroughly reworked a garment for the upper body.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor hat is a type of headgear, which is worn on top of the head.

clue.text: Female deity's found in group of goddesses

parts.note: Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin, and the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: A female god turns up in a company of divinities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' is a link phrase, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fates are the three Greek goddesses who spin, measure and cut the thread of life.

clue.text: Perform movements appropriately for Water Music?

definitions.text: Perform movements appropriately for Water Music?

parts.words: Perform movements appropriately for Water Music?
parts.note: Water Music is Handel's suite, but water from the tap suggests a dance done with metal-plated shoes

explanation.surface: Dancers choreograph steps to Handel's Water Music.
explanation.walkthrough: Tap water plus dance: a fitting dance for 'water' music.
explanation.definitionFit: Tap dancing is rhythmic stepping in metal-tipped shoes, punning on tap water.

clue.text: Strategically delay work in theatre on behalf of great physician

parts.note: a play is a work staged in a theatre
for means on behalf of
time is the great healer, as the proverb has it

explanation.surface: A stage work about a renowned doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: To play for time is to stall deliberately, an idiom for strategic delaying.

clue.text: Sign up as submariner

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an omen is a sign of things to come

explanation.surface: Someone enlists to serve on a submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link word. Captain Nemo commands the submarine Nautilus in Jules Verne's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Nemo is Jules Verne's famous submarine captain, a fictional submariner.

clue.text: It makes a lot of money when normality is disrupted

definitions.text: It makes a lot of money

indicators.note: the letters of normality are thrown into disorder and reassembled

explanation.surface: A firm profits handsomely whenever ordinary life is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link word. The British state body that strikes coins and so literally makes money.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Mint is the UK institution that manufactures coins, so it produces money in quantity.

clue.text: Job is finished before the first such work appears

definitions.text: Job is finished before the first such work appears

parts.words: Job is finished before the first such work appears
parts.note: in the Bible the Book of Job ends and the next book opens with the first of its hymns, so 'Job' is the book, not employment

explanation.surface: One task must be completed before a new piece of work can begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Job' at the start of the clue hides its capital: it is the Old Testament book that directly precedes the Book of Psalms.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalm is a sacred song, and the Book of Psalms follows Job in the Old Testament.

clue.text: Labour group with minimal membership

parts.note: a workforce cut to the bare bones, with a pun on membership as limbs, the members of a body

explanation.surface: A trade union or Labour faction that has very few members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' suggests the political party; it simply means work, and a skeleton is all bones with no flesh.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton staff is the smallest number of workers needed to keep an operation running.

clue.text: New York politician in Ireland, say

indicators.note: in means the politician goes inside the name for Ireland

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
an MP is a Member of Parliament
say here means state, to declare

explanation.surface: A New York politician visiting Ireland makes a statement.
explanation.definitionFit: The Empire State is the traditional nickname of New York State.

clue.text: New state norms for classification

indicators.note: new means the letters of state and norms are formed afresh

explanation.surface: Newly drafted state rules for sorting things.
explanation.definitionFit: An assortment is a sorting into kinds, and also the varied group that results, a synonym for classification.

clue.text: Predecessor or successor of Alexander

parts.note: any ... Alexander was preceded and followed by a pontiff, and the poet Alexander has this surname coming after his first name

explanation.surface: A question about who came before or after a king called Alexander.
explanation.walkthrough: Alexander suggests the Macedonian king; think instead of the popes named Alexander and of the poet Alexander Pope (1688-1744).
explanation.definitionFit: Popes named Alexander had fellow pontiffs before and after them, and the surname follows the poet's given name Alexander.

clue.text: Big game, restricted to first half to make money

definitions.text: Big game, restricted to first half to make money

parts.words: Big game, restricted to first half to make money
parts.note: the animal is a big-game quarry, and cutting its name to the first five letters leaves old British slang for cash

explanation.surface: A big match where only the first half is played, to earn money.
explanation.walkthrough: RHINO is old British slang for money, and it is the first half of this ten-letter animal's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhinoceros is one of the classic big-game animals hunted on safari.

clue.text: Points one repeated, warning journalists

parts.note: N, E, W and S are the four compass points
one of those points, west, is given a second time
an omen is a warning sign

explanation.surface: Someone notes several times over a warning to reporters.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma after 'Points' is missing, so 'one repeated' reads as part of the points: the west point is simply given twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Newswomen are female reporters, a kind of journalist.

clue.text: Tame variations for fellow player

indicators.note: variations means the letters are given different arrangements

parts.note: taken as written, the letters of tame
the plural variations asks for two versions of tame, so the word is used twice

explanation.surface: A domestic piece of music played in variations by fellow musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variations' is plural, so the eight letters of two copies of 'Tame' are shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: A teammate is someone on the same side as you, a fellow player.

clue.text: Bookmaker originally went to Ludlow or Taunton, perhaps

parts.note: St Mark wrote the second Gospel, so he made a book of the Bible

indicators.note: done in an original, inventive way, so the letters of went to are rearranged

explanation.surface: A turf accountant first went to two English country towns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bookmaker' suggests a betting shop, but it is the Gospel writer. 'originally' rearranges WENT TO into ETTOWN. Ludlow and Taunton are English towns with traditional markets.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludlow and Taunton are examples of English towns that hold a regular market.

clue.text: European's greeting American agents with love

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone from Europe welcomes US spies affectionately.
explanation.definitionFit: Ciao is the Italian informal hello or goodbye, so a greeting used by a European.

clue.text: Insufficient amount of resistance, in end

indicators.note: in means the resistance letter goes inside the word for end

parts.note: death is the end of life
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: Too little opposition at the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A dearth is a scarcity or lack, an insufficient amount of something.

clue.text: Part of uniform of South American judoist, say

indicators.note: say tells us the phrase is heard, not written, so the extra E of the surname is silent

parts.note: S for South and AM for American, then a brown belt is a fairly advanced judo grade

explanation.surface: A judo player from South America wears this as part of his kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks a homophone: S AM BROWN BELT sounds exactly like the strap named after General Sam Browne, whose surname has an E.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sam Browne belt, with a strap over the shoulder, is worn by army officers as part of uniform.

clue.text: Founder of city ancient civilisation put up

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: Sumer was the ancient civilisation of southern Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: The founder of a city built an ancient civilisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Remus and his twin Romulus are the legendary founders of Rome.

clue.text: Sign of the cross

parts.note: not the religious gesture but the arithmetic symbol shaped like a small cross

explanation.surface: The gesture made by a Christian blessing themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: The addition symbol is an upright cross, so it is literally a sign shaped like one.

clue.text: Source of wool a shopping centre returned

indicators.note: returned means the pair a and the shopping centre are read backwards as a single run

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: Someone brings wool back to a shopping centre.
explanation.definitionFit: The llama is a South American animal kept for its fleece, which is spun into wool.

clue.text: The writer having confidence about book is noteworthy

parts.note: the writer refers to the setter, who calls themself me

indicators.note: about means the word for confidence goes around the abbreviation for book

parts.note: morale is a group's confidence or spirit

explanation.surface: An author with self-belief about their book thinks it notable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something memorable is worth remembering, a close synonym of noteworthy.

clue.text: Set of changes in line of verse

definitions.meaning: in bell-ringing a ... is a call that alters the sequence of changes
a ... is a short line in a stanza, as in the ... and wheel of Sir Gawain

explanation.surface: A sequence of variations in a single line of poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word. Change-ringing is the English art of ringing church bells in shifting orders.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob names both a bell-ringing variation and a very short line in verse, two specialist senses.

clue.text: Author among greatest —- even so, neglected

indicators.note: among says the answer lies within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A writer, though one of the greats, is still overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across greaTEST EVEN SO Neglected. Robert Louis Stevenson wrote Treasure Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson is a famous Scottish author, so the surname names a writer.

clue.text: Breaking this is hard, to some extent

definitions.text: Breaking this is hard, to some extent

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
a bit means to some extent, slightly

explanation.surface: Kicking this is difficult, at least somewhat.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a habit is hard to break, and H plus A BIT builds it.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is an ingrained routine, notoriously difficult to break.
